headlines.title: King tides, strong waves destroy part of Pacifica pier as officials warn of coastal flooding
headlines.description: Santa Cruz and Capitola avoided serious damage Wednesday as powerful waves battered the coastline. In Santa Cruz, video posted on social media by the Santa Cruz World Surfing Reserve showed waves crashing over the metal railing near the wharf. No damage was reported. A high surf warning issued for the Pacific coast is set to expire at the end of Wednesday. City beaches in Santa Cruz will remain closed until 5 a.m. Thursday. “When the weather service tells us that the warning rises to the level that it poses a risk to public safety, meaning that surf is so strong it could pull people out and make it really challenging for our first responders to rescue them, we close the beaches,” Santa Cruz Emergency Services Manager Meredith Albert said. Hazardous beach conditions could linger through Monday, Albert said. “Understand that the ocean is a really strong force,” she said. Pacifica 10 hours ago weather 11 hours ago In Capitola, waves crashed over the seawall, coming close to businesses in Capitola Village, but no major flooding was reported. The dangerous surf did take a toll on business in the popular village. “Today, it’s supposed to be super busy because it’s the beginning of Thanksgiving, but it’s still a little bit slow,” restaurant owner Melissa Serriteno said. “Just come down to the village and support all the businesses. We really need it, especially the whole village.”
